additional_logical_suppliers.disposition: Defines an experiment as a measurable sample space, parameter labels, and a family of sampling laws; used by the finite tree-experiment definition.
States that the identity parameter target is identifiable exactly when the parameter-to-law map is injective; used by the split/coverage theorem and Gaussian-delay example.

Defines conditional latent-law calculation followed by maximization of expected complete-data log density; finite-state specialization used by the local link-loss algorithm. Its separate AC/KL branch and ascent theorem are not invoked.
Defines N(mu,1) as a shifted standard-normal law and assumes AC; used only by the normal-delay B example.
AC is carried only in the Gaussian example because the cited normal-law definition assumes it. No AC is used by the finite Bernoulli model, EM sums, or split/coverage theorem.

item_arguments_and_dependencies.claim_and_conventions: Defines finite rooted tree, nonroot branching convention, finite receiver subsets and counts, independent homogeneous Bernoulli link successes, full path-product outcome vectors, their finite-state probability law, and pattern counts.
Defines receiver coverage and nonroot internal-vertex splitting by a single receiver set meeting two child subtrees; makes no identifiability theorem claim.

Finite-state EM procedure with link-coverage and data-feasibility checks, conditional expected latent link successes, expected successes divided by probes traversing each edge, and likelihood-tolerance/iteration-cap statuses. It asserts no convergence or global optimum.

For p_e in (0,1), prove full repeated-probe law injectivity iff all leaves are covered and every nonroot internal vertex is split. Sufficiency uses q_r leaf marginals, q_v=m_r m_s/m_rs at each split, and p_(u,v)=q_v/q_u. Necessity uses an unobserved leaf edge or a small incoming/outgoing probability rescaling at an unsplit node.

Independent N(mu_i,1) delays on a shared-edge two-leaf tree give pointwise equal coupled path sums for mean vectors (0,0,0) and (1,-1,-1); carries AC only because the local normal-law definition assumes it.
